as_reported: Biallelic variants in the COQ7 gene

records.label: Patient II-2

phenotypes.text: distal upper limb weakness of hands
amyotrophy of lower limbs and hands
pure motor axonal neuropathy on ENMG with fibrillations and neurogenic pattern

records.segregation: homozygous in all three affected sibs; heterozygous in unaffected parents
quotes: The index case, Patient II-2, was a 36-year-old man (Fig. 1A).
When he was 12 years old, he developed walking difficulties with a sensation of stiffness in the lower limbs and a difficulty walking on heels.
Deep tendon reflexes were brisk in the four limbs (except for Achilles reflexes which were abolished), and a Hoffman’s sign was found, without Babinski’s sign or spasticity.

records.label: Patient II-3

phenotypes.text: difficulty feeling cold and warm on feet
pure motor axonal neuropathy on ENMG

records.segregation: homozygous in all three affected sibs; heterozygous in unaffected parents
quotes: Patient II-3 was a 25-year-old woman. She had normal early development, without walking difficulty when she was a child. When she was 9 years old, she developed walking difficulties with fatigability and feet drop.
She complained of difficulties in feeling cold and warm temperatures on her feet.
Deep tendon reflexes were found to be normal in the four limbs, and no Hoffman’s sign was found, but a Babinski’s sign was found on the left foot.

records.label: Patient II-1

phenotypes.text: severe distal lower limb and hand amyotrophy

records.segregation: homozygous in all three affected sibs; heterozygous in unaffected parents
quotes: Patient II-1 was a 42-year-old man.
When he was 10 years old, he noticed walking and biking difficulties, particularly when compared to his classmates, with foot drop.
Clinical examination showed a severe amyotrophy in lower limbs, with a distal predominance, and an amyotrophy of hand muscles.

records.label: Five new patients with COQ7-related primary CoQ10 deficiency
quotes: We identified five new patients with COQ7-related primary CoQ10 deficiency, performed clinical assessment of the patients

The main clinical features included a neonatal-onset presentation with severe neuromuscular, cardiorespiratory and renal involvement and a late-onset disease presenting with progressive neuropathy, lower extremity weakness, abnormal gait, and variable developmental delay.

notes.statement: Wongkittichote et al. (2023) described two distinct presentations of COQ7-related primary CoQ10 deficiency. One was neonatal onset with severe neuromuscular, cardiorespiratory, and renal involvement. The other was late onset with progressive neuropathy, lower extremity weakness, abnormal gait, and variable developmental delay. The authors noted an emerging genotype-phenotype correlation.
quotes: The main clinical features included a neonatal-onset presentation with severe neuromuscular, cardiorespiratory and renal involvement and a late-onset disease presenting with progressive neuropathy, lower extremity weakness, abnormal gait, and variable developmental delay.
Overall, we define two distinct disease presentations of COQ7-related disorder with emerging genotype-phenotype correlation

notes.statement: Wongkittichote et al. (2023) found that a yeast strain lacking CAT5, the COQ7 ortholog (cat5-delta), could not grow on oxidative carbon sources. Wildtype CAT5 fully rescued this defect, but CAT5 carrying the equivalents of human pathogenic variants did not. Equivalents of the human R54Q, R107W, and I66N variants and of the complex allele [T103M;L111P] partially rescued growth, indicating that these are hypomorphic alleles.
quotes: Expression of wild-type CAT5 could completely rescue the defect; however, yeast CAT5 harboring equivalent human pathogenic variants could not.

cat5Δ yeast harboring p.Arg57Gln (equivalent to human p.Arg54Gln), p.Arg112Trp (equivalent to p.Arg107Trp), p.Ile69Asn (equivalent to p.Ile66Asn) and combination of p.Lys108Met and p.Leu116Pro (equivalent to the complex allele p.[Thr103Met;Leu111Pro]) partially rescued the growth defects, indicating these variants are hypomorphic alleles.

notes.statement: In the yeast model, Wongkittichote et al. (2023) found that supplementation with 2,4-dihydroxybenzoic acid rescued the growth defect of both the leaky and the severe COQ7-equivalent mutants. Overexpressing COQ8 together with 2,4-diHB supplementation restored oxidative growth and the respiratory defect, and the two acted synergistically.
quotes: Supplementation with 2,4 dihydroxybenzoic acid (2,4-diHB) rescued the growth defect of both the leaky and severe mutants. Overexpression of COQ8 and 2,4-diHB supplementation synergistically restored oxidative growth and respiratory defect.

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2023) found that the COQ7 c.1A>G variant was absent from gnomAD and predicted to abolish the initiating methionine, so that translation would start at methionine 39, removing the cleavable mitochondrial targeting sequence and 2 more amino acids.
quotes: The COQ7 variant was absent in gnomAD, and in silico prediction modeling predicted pathogenicity.
is expected to bypass the first 38 amino acid residues at the n-terminus, initiating instead with methionine at position 39

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2023) found that fibroblasts from affected sibs had severely reduced COQ7 protein, 87% lower CoQ10, and accumulated DMQ10, which was absent in cells from the carrier father and sib. Muscle and fibroblasts showed impaired maximal respiration. Muscle also showed increased H2O2 emission and fewer complex I- and IV-containing supercomplexes.
quotes: On average, cultured fibroblasts from siblings 1, 2, and 3 had 87% lower CoQ10 than their father and unaffected sibling
with COQ7 to porin ratios 85% ± 7% lower in affected siblings than their carrier father and sibling 4
Simultaneous fluorometric analysis demonstrated higher H2O2 emissions in muscle from sibling 2 compared with those in muscle from healthy controls

notes.statement: Smith et al. (2023) noted that, unlike previously reported COQ7-related CoQ10 deficiency, their patients had a pure length-dependent motor neuropathy without sensory involvement, demyelination, developmental delay or upper motor neuron signs. Deafness in the family was explained by homozygous GJB2 variants and did not segregate with the COQ7 variant.
quotes: The siblings had no developmental delay or cognitive impairment and no upper motor neuron features.
hearing loss did not segregate with COQ7 variants in this report. In this family, deafness was explained by the pathogenic homozygous c35delG p.(GLy12Valfs*2) variants in GJB2.

notes.statement: Liu et al. (2023) reported that biallelic variants in the COQ7 gene caused distal hereditary motor neuropathy in 2 Chinese families.
quotes: Biallelic variants in the COQ7 gene cause distal hereditary motor neuropathy in two Chinese families.

notes.statement: Jacquier et al. (2023) reported that the family, with affected sibs born to nonconsanguineous healthy Portuguese parents, displayed an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern.
quotes: The affected siblings were born from non-consanguineous healthy parents in Portugal (Table 1). The family displayed an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern.

notes.statement: In 3 sibs with distal hereditary motor neuropathy, Jacquier et al. (2023) identified by whole-exome sequencing a homozygous c.3G>T substitution in the start codon of COQ7 isoform 1 (p.Met1?), which segregated with the disorder; the variant was present once in heterozygous state in gnomAD. Alternative isoforms 2 and 3 use other start codons and were predicted to be unaffected.
quotes: only one variant, which was absent from the ExAC database but present once at the heterogenous state in gnomAD database (allele frequency 0.000004065) was shared by the three patients in a homozygous state and present in their unaffected parents in a heterozygous state
Interestingly, two alternative start codons are used by isoforms 2 and 3, indicating that these two alternative isoforms should not be affected by the variant.

notes.statement: Jacquier et al. (2023) found that the c.3G>T mutation reduced COQ7 protein levels by 85% in transfected SH-EP neuroblastoma cells without changing mRNA levels or subcellular localization, and COQ7 protein was barely detectable in patient fibroblasts, consistent with a translation initiation defect. A FLAG-tagged isoform 2 localized to mitochondria, suggesting partial compensation.
quotes: COQ7 levels were reduced by 85% in SH-EP cells expressing the mutant COQ7 compared to SH-EP cells expressing the wild-type COQ7
COQ7 protein was barely detected in the patient’s fibroblasts, whereas it was easily detected in control cells (Fig. 3B), suggesting a drastic reduction in the COQ7 protein level.
Immunostaining of the Flag and mitochondrial protein TOM20 showed that COQ7 isoform 2 was expressed and co-localized with mitochondria

notes.statement: Jacquier et al. (2023) found decreased CoQ10 (12.5 vs 71.5 pmol/mg protein) and accumulation of 6-demethoxy-CoQ10 (6-DMQ), the COQ7 substrate, in patient fibroblasts, and 6-DMQ was also detected in patient plasma. The CoQ10 precursor 2,4-dihydroxybenzoic acid slightly increased CoQ10 and normalized 6-DMQ in fibroblasts.
quotes: We observed a major decrease in the CoQ10 level from 71.5 pmol/mg of protein in control fibroblasts to 12.5 pmol/mg of protein in patient fibroblasts together with the appearance of 6-DMQ in the fibroblasts of the patient compared with the controls
The appearance of 6-DMQ was also found in the patient’s plasma (Fig. 4B).
The results indicated that 2,4-dHB slightly increased CoQ10 levels from 12.5 to 18.8 pmol/mg and normalized 6-DMQ accumulation in the patient’s fibroblasts

notes.statement: Jacquier et al. (2023) showed that patient fibroblasts had reduced mitochondrial ATP production with compensatory increase in glycolysis, reduced basal and maximal respiration rescued by CoQ10 supplementation, and reduced proliferation in galactose medium that was partially rescued by 10 microM CoQ10.
quotes: Both basal and maximal respirations were significantly reduced in fibroblasts carrying the c.3G>T mutation (Fig. 4H). Interestingly, these basal and maximal respiration rates could be rescued by CoQ10 supplementation
Cell counting revealed that CoQ10 supplementation induced a 100% increase in the number of COQ7 mutated fibroblasts after 3 days (Fig. 5E).

notes.statement: Jacquier et al. (2023) speculated that the milder pure dHMN phenotype, compared with the severe multisystem COQ10D8 phenotypes caused by catalytic-domain COQ7 mutations affecting all isoforms, resulted from the start-codon mutation affecting only isoform 1 and not completely preventing CoQ10 synthesis.
quotes: We speculate that in our patient the mutation affects only the translation of the main COQ7 isoform, and does not affect the two other COQ7 isoforms, and as a consequence does not completely prevent CoQ10 synthesis.
Consistently, all previously described COQ7 mutations were localized in the catalytic site and therefore affected all COQ7 isoforms.

notes.statement: Jacquier et al. (2023) described the disorder as a length-dependent pure motor axonal neuropathy with childhood onset and progressive walking difficulties; pyramidal features suggested upper motor neuron involvement. In one patient, brain and spinal MRI, echocardiography, ECG, and audiometry were normal, and CPK was mildly elevated.
quotes: All of the patients presented with length-dependent pure motor axonal neuropathy, leading to progressive walking difficulties and disability, with childhood onset.
The clinical phenotype of dHMN with pyramidal features reported here is suggestive of upper motor neuron involvement.
Biological testing showed a mild elevation of the creatine phosphokinase (CPK) level (215 U/l, normal <200 U/l).

notes.statement: Jacquier et al. (2023) noted that one patient reported symptom stabilization between ages 15 and 18 years while treated with CoQ10 (30 mg/day), with renewed worsening after stopping, and proposed oral CoQ10 supplementation as a potential therapy; plasma 6-DMQ accumulation could confirm pathogenicity of COQ7 variants.
quotes: Between 15 and 18 years of age, while she was treated with CoQ10 (30 mg per day), she reported symptom stabilization. A new progressive worsening started at the age of 18 years and the stop of CoQ10 supplementation.
When COQ7 variants are identified, the accumulation of 6-DMQ levels in the plasma observed herein will be useful to confirm the pathogenicity of these variants.
